approachQuestion.prompt:
Gallery Index. Return all unique gallery IDs from a binary layout in this order: all IDs of its left subtree under the same rule, then the current ID, then all IDs of its right subtree. Numeric ID order has no relationship to the layout. The input supplies n and a writable output array of length n; fill and return it.

In examples, x(left,right) denotes a node labelled x, and - denotes an absent child. Example 1: Input: 40(70(-,10(-,-)),20(-,-)). Output: [70,10,40,20]. Example 2: Input: 8(-,3(-,6(-,-))). Output: [8,3,6]. Example 3: Input: -. Output: [].

Constraints: 0 <= n <= 200000; IDs are unique signed 32-bit integers. The immutable tree has child pointers only and no cycles or shared nodes. Shape is unrestricted. The supplied output buffer contains only the final sequence; its unwritten slots are not available as workspace.

options.text: Follow left children, pushing nodes. When the current pointer is missing, pop a node, emit its ID into the next output slot, and continue from its right child.
options.feedback: A node stays pending until its left subtree is finished, then it precedes its right subtree.

options.text: Use that left-current-right traversal but append IDs to a separate linked list, then copy the list into the supplied output array.
options.feedback: The order is correct for every tree. The extra sequence and final copy are removable by writing each ID directly to its final output slot.

options.text: Visit nodes in any order, fill the output, then sort it numerically.
options.feedback: No search-tree property is given. Example 1 requires [70,10,40,20], not [10,20,40,70].

options.text: For each k from 1 to n, restart the left-current-right traversal at the root, stop at its kth visited node, and emit just that ID.
options.feedback: This is correct brute force but replays the same prefixes unnecessarily. A single traversal already visits all output positions in order.

feedback.reason: Emit a node only after its left subtree; label order is independent of structural order.
details: Keep a current pointer, node stack, and output index. Push nodes while moving left. At a missing pointer, pop a node, write its ID into the next output slot, and move to its right child. Continue while the pointer exists or the stack is non-empty. Return the buffer.

Descending left defers every ancestor until its left subtree finishes. Popping emits that ancestor before moving right. The explicit stack stores unfinished traversal obligations, not a second copy of the returned ID list.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the revealed pointer-stack method let n >= 1 be the node count and h the longest root-to-leaf path length in nodes. Choose the tight worst-case pair. Count the stack and scalar pointers/index; exclude the input and supplied final output array. Each output write takes constant time without resizing or copying.
constraints: All legal shapes are allowed; do not assume balance. Heights count nodes, not edges.

Pointer access, comparisons, arithmetic on the stated integer ranges, and allocation/release of a fixed-size frame take constant time. No hashing is used. Count all live explicit frames; the method does not use language recursion or copy paths/subtrees unless explicitly stated.

feedback.reason: Each node is pushed, popped, and emitted once; pending ancestors determine space.
details: Every node is pushed, popped, and emitted once. At most h ancestors are pending, and a left chain attains h stack entries.
Before a node is popped its left subtree is complete. Emitting that node and then visiting its right subtree preserves the required order at every subtree.
“O(n) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Every node is pushed, popped, and emitted once. At most h ancestors are pending, and a left chain attains h stack entries.
“O(n²) time, O(h) auxiliary space”: Completed subtrees are not scanned again; nesting the control flow does not itself multiply the node visits.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The live explicit stack is auxiliary memory and can grow with tree height.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: This is a looser upper bound since h <= n; the height-sensitive bound is tighter and no full node table is retained.
